messages.author: 8012f85b52dee887
messages.subject: rsf.select output and projection issues
parts:
Hi All,

I've been trying to conduct rsf.select on bird home ranges (93 to 378 telemetry locations).

I'm using the cropland raster (https://croplandcros.scinet.usda.gov/) to see what habitats the birds select.  I'm running into issues where my output (the summary function) shows each category as having an est of NaN.

In addition, I am trying to run continuous rasters (percent canopy cover and percent impervious surface), and for some home ranges they are not showing up as having a coefficient (it just shows area, T[position], T[velocity], etc.).

For all rasters, I made sure they matched the projection of the telemetry objects (the bird movebank points and the wAKDE), and I made sure the crop raster was a factor.  I also clipped the rasters to encompass the entire home range with a buffer.

Here is the code I use:

rsf_can_799 <- ctmm:::rsf.select(bird_799, UD=wAKDE_799, R=list(canopy=canopy_799),
                                 debias=TRUE, error=0.05, trace=TRUE, level.UD=0.95)
summary(rsf_can_799)


rsf_imp_799 <- ctmm:::rsf.select(bird_799, UD=wAKDE_799, R=list(imp=imp_799),
                                 debias=TRUE, error=0.05, trace=TRUE, level.UD=0.95)
summary(rsf_imp_799)

rsf_crop_799 <- ctmm:::rsf.select(bird_799, UD=wAKDE_799, R=list(crop=crop_799),
                                  debias=TRUE, error=0.05, trace=TRUE, level.UD=0.95,
                                  integrator="Riemann")

summary(rsf_crop_799)

If anyone had a similar problem or could provide guidance, it would be greatly appreciated!!!

I feel like I've tried everything to no avail.

Thank you!

messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: rsf.select output and projection issues
parts:
Hi Megan,

If you don't see any covariates after running rsf.select(), then it's because none were selected for those individuals. rsf.fit() will force an estimate (which will have CIs far overlapping zero), but then the covariance estimate is not numerically reliable for the population estimate via mean().

If you see a bunch of NaN in categorical coefficients, it's usually because of collinearity, such as if all locations fall into one category. If that's not the case, then I can take a look at it.

Best,
Chris

messages.subject: Re: rsf.select output and projection issues
parts:
I should also add that the MonteCarlo integrator seems to be less sensitive to collinearity than the faster Riemann integrator.

Best,
Chris
